newsitem.title: CANADA: TCPL, Northern States plan US$1 bln gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: TCPL, Northern States plan US$1 bln gas pipeline.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and Northern States Power Co said on Wednesday they planned to seek regulatory approval for a US$1 billion natural gas pipeline in the U.S. midwest.
The companies said the proposed 800-mile Viking Voyageur Gas Transmission project would be designed to ship up to 1.2 billion cubic feet of gas a day to U.S. midwest markets by late 1999.

Voyageur would follow the pipeline corridor of NSP's Viking Gas Transmission line to provide links to Minnesota, Wisconsin and Illinois markets from an interconnection with TransCanada's mainline at Emerson, Manitoba, they said.
The firms said they expected to file an application for the project with the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in the autumn, after an open season to be held in May.
The project is the latest in a multibillion-dollar string of expansion plans for Calgary-based TransCanada, which have been dubbed the Nexus project.
The company, along with partner Coastal Corp, announced plans two weeks ago to expand their Great Lakes Gas Transmission pipeline in the northern Unites States at a cost of US$2.5 billion.

TransCanada's plans are calculated to compete with the proposed Alliance Pipeline project, backed by a group of Canadian producers, which would ship 1.3 billion cubic feet per day to Chicago from northeastern British Columbia.
"The project's strong market orientation fits nicely with TransCanada's proposed Nexus expansion," TransCanada Chief Executive George Watson said in a statement.
"We think our integrated package offers customers a wider variety of choices and benefits than the Alliance proposal."
TransCanada and NSP said early discussions with market players produced strong indications of support for the Voyageur project.
Several local distribution companies in Wisconsin expressed intentions to support the project by adding the necessary connections with their own distribution systems, the firms said.
As part of the proposal, TransCanada would have the right to acquire a 50 percent stake in Viking Gas Transmission, it said.
